findings.title: ONNX-only SAM checkpoints need contract-derived composite discovery without replacing native PyTorch SAM export
findings.observation: At Xenova/slimsam-77-uniform revision 5850ab45f587c112167512ffef949107115e26a0, the checkpoint has no PyTorch weights and publishes two cooperating fp32 ONNX graphs: vision_encoder.onnx SHA-256 9f8433273a6750b587779baa0cf5508111001bf7e7acfcf585d370139fd366d0 and prompt_encoder_mask_decoder.onnx SHA-256 f4514391764fbd56e08e119060d874ecd7d52994bfb1968af159e12d4943b5bb. Generic graph-I/O discovery resolves them as image-encoder and prompt-decoder, emits portable component_name recipes, and builds all four CPU artifacts. The repaired optional-source fallback also preserves facebook/sam-vit-base as the existing single PyTorch config path when no published ONNX pair exists; six focused source-selection/composite tests passed.

gotchas: Do not register an optional published-ONNX composite in a way that replaces the existing native PyTorch path when discovery returns no sources.
Malformed or ambiguous published pairs must fail closed; only the no-published-pair case falls through to PyTorch export.
Keep Hub cache paths out of recipes; persist the semantic component_name and resolve the pinned published graph during build.
findings.mechanism_notes: Fresh tester re-entry proved Xenova composite fan-out and the facebook native-source fallback independently; deliverable SHA-256 026c4b99a5325d49447689dee52da4aa2425ca26027a16c40ddcb058be432383 and terminal tester verdict SHA-256 e88be8c3482bfd7702114bfa2db065ce7eacc52ce9c1255f3044c0f7dea421cf freeze the repaired behavior.

findings.title: SlimSAM is a two-graph point-prompt composite, and direct ONNX ingestion emits no HTP trace metadata
findings.observation: The frozen model profile records a 9,723,528-parameter SAM configuration with a 12-block width-168 vision encoder (global attention at blocks 2, 5, 8, 11), 256-channel neck, point-prompt encoder, and two-layer width-256 two-way-transformer mask decoder. Frozen artifact I/O confirms the runtime boundary: pixel_values FLOAT[B,3,1024,1024] -> image_embeddings and image_positional_embeddings FLOAT[B,256,64,64]; the decoder consumes those tensors plus input_points FLOAT[B,point_batch,points,2] and input_labels INT64[B,point_batch,points], then emits iou_scores FLOAT[B,point_batch,3] and pred_masks FLOAT[B,point_batch,3,256,256]. No export_htp_metadata.json exists for any of the four artifacts because export=null direct ONNX ingestion bypasses HTPExporter; therefore no total_modules/modules_traced/execution_steps claim is made. Architecture evidence is instead the pinned config/source-derived model-breakdown plus graph I/O, node scopes, and topology.

findings.title: SlimSAM recipes are direct-ONNX role configs; fp16 is a genuine conversion with a default-ORT optimizer caveat
findings.observation: All resolved configs have auto=false, export=null, optim={}, compile=null, and portable loader.component_name. fp32 quant is null. fp16 uses quant.mode=fp16 with fp16_keep_io_types=true. The fp32 encoder is 27,313,796 bytes with 184 FLOAT initializers; fp16 is 13,899,113 bytes with 184 FLOAT16 and zero FLOAT initializers. The fp32 decoder is 16,519,175 bytes with 137 FLOAT initializers; fp16 is 8,400,644 bytes with 137 FLOAT16 and zero FLOAT initializers. Both fp16 graphs preserve FLOAT I/O but fail default ORT session initialization at InsertedPrecisionFreeCast/SimplifiedLayerNormFusion; both initialize and execute with ORT_DISABLE_ALL. Standard winml perf therefore exits 2, while the composite ORT_DISABLE_ALL harness passes.
gotchas: The checkpoint's published fp16 variants are not the validated sources; convert the exact published fp32 pair through WinML.
A successful fp16 build is insufficient: verify FLOAT16 initializer counts and session creation.
On this runtime, ORT_DISABLE_ALL is required for fp16 and makes CPU fp16 slower than fp32; do not claim a speedup from reduced storage.
feature_gaps_filed: FILE: src/winml/modelkit/commands/perf.py — expose a graph-optimization/session-options override so converted SAM fp16 graphs can run standard winml perf with ORT_DISABLE_ALL
findings.mechanism_notes: Initializer dtypes, file-size ratios, default-vs-disabled session A/B checks, and full composite execution independently confirm both genuine conversion and the optimizer-specific failure.

findings.title: Incomplete pattern metadata must reject only that match rather than abort SAM analysis
findings.observation: The first analyzer pass aborted all four artifacts with KeyError 'X' because dtype-dependent LayerNormalization validation received a partial external-input mapping. The generic Pattern._check_skeleton_result_impl repair rejects only an unprovable pattern match when a matched external input lacks value/shape/type-derived data; it does not fabricate a classification and analysis continues. The refreshed public-rules v0.2.0 runs emitted valid JSON for all four artifacts and every requested target. Broad affected-area validation passed 3012 tests with 45 skipped; changed/untracked Python Ruff and git diff --check also passed.

validated_on: Xenova/slimsam-77-uniform @ fp32/fp16 image-encoder and prompt-decoder @ public analyze rules v0.2.0
not_yet_tested_on: other dtype-dependent pattern families with missing external-input metadata

gotchas: A missing metadata key disproves only that pattern match; it does not justify aborting graph-wide analysis.
Do not turn incomplete metadata into a positive or negative operator-support claim.
Analyzer exit 1 can still be ANALYZE-PARTIAL-SUCCESS when complete fail-closed JSON is emitted for all requested targets.
findings.mechanism_notes: A/B evidence is the deterministic KeyError before repair versus four complete 11-target outputs after repair, backed by a generic regression and broad analyzer suite.

findings.title: SlimSAM static analysis covers four artifacts and all 11 EP/device rule targets with role-stable operator profiles
findings.observation: Public rules v0.2.0 (SHA-256 6dcabbe7f5493fbc2bd23de195ab6e35b3578d510f18c2e220bc5538a1f232cc; 1746 parquet files) produced ANALYZE-PARTIAL-SUCCESS for all four artifacts. fp32 encoder: 1782 nodes/26 types, top three Unsqueeze=245, Add=201, Mul=166, mapped 1775/1782 (99.6072%). fp16 encoder: 1785/26, same top three, mapped 1775/1785 (99.4398%). fp32 decoder: 810/32, top three Gather=137, Unsqueeze=124, Add=93, mapped 809/810 (99.8765%). fp16 decoder: 815/32, same top three, mapped 809/815 (99.2638%). Every artifact contains these 11 target rows: NvTensorRTRTX/GPU; CUDA/GPU; MIGraphX/GPU; QNN/NPU; QNN/GPU; OpenVINO/NPU; OpenVINO/GPU; OpenVINO/CPU; Dml/GPU; CPU/CPU; VitisAI/NPU. Encoder rows are precision-stable: NvTensorRTRTX 12 supported/0 partial/0 unsupported/25 unknown; CUDA 0/0/0/26; MIGraphX 0/0/0/26; QNN NPU 10/3/0/25 (partial Mod, Reshape, Transpose); QNN GPU 10/2/0/25 (partial Mod, Transpose); OpenVINO NPU 6/1/5/25 (partial Sub; unsupported Mod, Add, Div, Mul, Cast); OpenVINO GPU and CPU each 6/0/6/25 (unsupported Mod, Sub, Add, Div, Mul, Cast); Dml, CPU, and VitisAI each 0/0/0/26. Decoder rows are also precision-stable: NvTensorRTRTX 8/0/0/32; CUDA and MIGraphX 0/0/0/32; QNN NPU and GPU 8/0/0/32; OpenVINO NPU, GPU, and CPU each 6/0/2/32 (unsupported Mul, Div); Dml, CPU, and VitisAI each 0/0/0/32. runtime_support=false for every static row, so none is runtime compatibility evidence.
